meta.title: The one list
meta.authority: This file is the ONLY record of what is done. Prose docs explain the work; they do not track it.
meta.howToRead:
pnpm backlog          — the working view (open + blocked)
pnpm backlog --lane owner — one lane
pnpm check:backlog    — prove every row against the tree (runs in CI)
rules: A row's status is proven by its verify probe, not by memory. If they disagree, CI fails.
A probe must measure the CONSEQUENCE in the tree, never restate the row's own title. A probe that passes by existing is the shape-not-truth failure this repo names in four ADRs.
Manual rows never fail the build (ADR-970). They carry evidence + a checked date and go stale loudly.
Parked rows are not probed: 'you could do this now' is true of everything parked and therefore says nothing.
Never delete a probe to make CI pass. That is precisely how the previous five master lists drifted.

lanes.hygiene: Debt in the record or the instruments.

entries.title: DECIDE the amber-button contrast fix: 8 midnight-dark contexts are carried as declared ceilings until then
entries.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-17 in CI, not estimated. The failing pair is WHITE TEXT ON THE AMBER BUTTON, not amber as text: #FFFFFF on #F0AD4E is 1.95:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement. Amber as TEXT is fine (#F0AD4E on the midnight-dark surface #161C28 is 8.77:1). 🔴 THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL REMEDY - 'swap to primary-strong' - IS A NO-OP IN MIDNIGHT-DARK. That skin sets --color-primary-strong to #F0AD4E, the SAME value as --color-primary, so the swap changes nothing. It works in midnight-LIGHT, where primary-strong is #8C5410 and white on it measures 6.19:1. Anyone applying the fix as written would see light mode go green, dark mode stay red, and reasonably conclude the guard was flaky. WHY IT SURFACED NOW: LIVE-008 fixed a selector that could never match, so midnight-dark paints its real palette instead of falling back to the generic .dark one. The failure is PRE-EXISTING and was invisible, not introduced. It costs 8 contexts on the a11y ratchet, all midnight-dark desktop, contrast only: /, /about, /discover, /pricing and /the-lab 0 -> 3; /the-quest 0 -> 4; /spaces 2 -> 6; /the-community 3 -> 7. TWO OPTIONS, both measured: (A) keep the brand amber and darken the FOREGROUND on it - #1C2535 on #F0AD4E is 7.90:1, #161C28 is 8.77:1. The brand colour is untouched and only the text on the button moves. (B) give midnight-dark a genuine primary-strong and keep white text - #7A4A0E gives 7.46:1, #8C5410 gives 6.19:1 (the value midnight-light already uses). (A) is the smaller change and preserves the accent exactly; (B) matches how the light skin already solves it. It is a BRAND decision either way, which is why it is not being made in code.

verify.evidence: Measured in CI 2026-08-17 (run 32077367930, `pnpm a11y:baselines`): 8 midnight-dark desktop contexts regressed, contrast only, and the capture REFUSED to raise the baselines rather than laundering the rise. Ratios computed from the tokens in app/globals.css: #FFFFFF on #F0AD4E = 1.95:1; #FFFFFF on #8C5410 = 6.19:1; #1C2535 on #F0AD4E = 7.90:1. Not repo-probeable: which remedy to take is a brand decision, and a probe asserting either one would force a choice the owner has not made.

entries.notes: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-18: WAIVE FOR NOW. The eight midnight-dark desktop contrast contexts are declared CEILINGS in test/e2e/a11y-baselines.json (/, /about, /discover, /pricing, /the-lab at 3; /the-quest 4; /spaces 6; /the-community 7), each carrying the measurement, both remedies, and the exact command that converts it back to a reading at 0. check:a11y-baselines prints every one of them on EVERY run - 'every ceiling is headroom a real regression can sit in while this prints a tick' - so the debt is carried in the open rather than hidden. This unblocks pr-compare without laundering a WCAG failure into a recorded fact. 🔴 THE ROW IS BLOCKED, NOT DONE. A known 1.95:1 pair is live in production on the amber button in midnight-dark. Both fixes are measured and one line each: (A) #1C2535 on #F0AD4E = 7.90:1, brand colour untouched; (B) --color-primary-strong #7A4A0E with white = 7.46:1, the shape midnight-LIGHT already uses. Whichever is picked, the eight ceilings retire in the same pass.

entries.title: Lift 8b: a loading prop on IconButton, matching Button's
entries.detail: Icon-only controls are exactly the ones where a tap leaves no other evidence it landed.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/ui/icon-button.tsx',T='components/ui/icon-button.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),test=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const cut=src.indexOf('export function IconLink');if(cut<0)process.exit(79);const B=src.slice(0,cut),L=src.slice(cut);function a(s,k){let i=0;while((i=s.indexOf(k+'={',i))>=0){const aria=s.slice(Math.max(0,i-5),i).endsWith('aria-');const e=s.indexOf('}',i);if(e>0&&s.slice(i,e).includes('loading')&&(k.indexOf('aria-')===0||!aria))return true;i+=k.length}return false}const bad=[];if(!a(B,'disabled'))bad.push('IconButton does not disable while loading; a second tap re-fires the action');if(!a(B,'aria-busy'))bad.push('IconButton does not set aria-busy while loading');if(!a(L,'aria-disabled'))bad.push('IconLink does not set aria-disabled while loading');if(!a(L,'aria-busy'))bad.push('IconLink does not set aria-busy while loading');if(!test.includes('does not fire the handler again'))bad.push('the double-fire assertion is gone from '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The probe that flagged this row as stale was `grep-present /loading/` in the component, which passes because the WORD appears anywhere in the file, including in a comment describing the prop it is supposed to be proving. Replaced with the consequence: IconButton must disable while loading (so a second tap cannot re-fire the action) and set aria-busy; IconLink must use the aria pair INSTEAD of the real `disabled`, because a real disabled drops it out of the tab order mid-navigation; and the double-fire assertion must still exist in the test file. ONE TRAP WORTH RECORDING: both controls live in one file and the string 'aria-disabled=' CONTAINS 'disabled=', so an unscoped regex let each component satisfy the other's check. Two of four deliberate breaks passed before that was caught, which is exactly why a probe is not trusted until it has been seen to fail. It now splits the file at IconLink and judges each half alone; all four breaks fire. A SECOND trap cost another round: the first scoped version used a regex, and this string travels JSON -> shell -> `node -e`, where a lone backslash does not survive intact - "\\b" arrived as a literal BACKSPACE, so every check silently matched nothing and the row read as regressed. The probe is now backslash-free, scanning with indexOf instead of RegExp, and was re-proved through the guard's own shell rather than only standalone.

entries.title: The .dark [data-skin="midnight"] selector never matches on the <html> path
entries.detail: A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself. app/layout.tsx stamps data-skin on documentElement (the global skin preview path, including marketing); only the shell root is a descendant. So midnight-dark renders a MIXTURE: the generic .dark palette with midnight's light-mode overrides under it. The comment at app/layout.tsx:142-143 asserts the opposite, which is why it survived. One selector, but it repaints every midnight-dark surface, so it wants its own pass with a baseline recapture.

entries.title: The app shell statically imports the entire admin module registry
entries.detail: settings-panel.tsx imports MODULE_COMPONENTS from components/admin/modules/module-map — a 'use client' pure registry with 38 static imports and no hooks, handlers or browser APIs. It reaches crypto-browserify/stream-browserify: 406 kB raw / 121 kB gzip on EVERY authed page, verified as a blocking script tag in served HTML. Fix: next/dynamic per module, import module IDS not components, and add import 'server-only' to lib/journey-plans and lib/practices so the class fails the build. NOTE: needs a route-level first-load measurement, which the agent container cannot produce (next build fails page-data collection without service-role creds).

entries.title: Sentry no longer ships to routes with no DSN configured
entries.detail: The static `import * as Sentry` is gone; the SDK is now reached through a dynamic import gated on process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN — the one env form the browser can resolve, since Next inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time. The server-only SENTRY_DSN fallback is deliberately NOT consulted here because it is never inlined into the browser bundle and could only read undefined. The hard part was the export contract: Next reads onRouterTransitionStart off this module's namespace and calls it on every client navigation, so it MUST stay defined with Sentry off — it is now a stable wrapper delegating to an async-loaded hook, with a .catch that leaves it a no-op if the chunk fails, because monitoring must never take down the app it monitors. Stated cost: a navigation in the first few ms of a configured session may go untraced. VERIFIED BEYOND THE ONE FILE (the searchSiteIcons lesson): every importer of lib/observability/sentry was enumerated — only sentry.server.config.ts and sentry.edge.config.ts import it statically, both server/edge runtimes, and lib/maps/diagnostics.ts deliberately reads the value without importing. No client component pulls it, so the SDK cannot re-enter the baseline chunk by a side door.
entries.notes: Artifact-verified 2026-08-17, not inferred: built with no DSN and read the emitted chunks. The 236,682-byte Sentry SDK chunk appears in 0 of 4,149 client entry lists across all 404 page_client-reference-manifest.js files, and the baseline chunk in rootMainFiles contains only the gated async loader. app/error, app/global-error and components/ui/route-error.tsx still import the SDK statically; Turbopack keeps those in async groups, so they are not a baseline regression and were deliberately left alone.

entries.title: Decide how /discover index pages resolve isAuthed without killing ISR
entries.detail: Three index pages call createClient() → cookies() purely for an isAuthed boolean, killing ISR and adding an auth round trip per crawl. DO NOT 'just remove the auth read' — it silently breaks sign-in destinations: isAuthed feeds communityHref, and proxy.ts builds its redirect by rewriting the pathname and NEVER setting next=, so the destination is lost. Two real options: (a) make the proxy set next= (strictly better product behaviour but changes where every signed-out deep link lands across 122 protected routes), or (b) resolve isAuthed client-side via the authMode="client" pattern app/discover/layout.tsx already uses. Same decision governs (main)/layout.tsx. Owner call.

entries.detail: app/globals.css removes the focus ring from the wordmark — the first tab stop on every page.

entries.title: The sitemap's batched podcast read was silently truncating at 1000 rows
entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS STALE AND THE REAL BUG WAS WORSE. The N+1 had already been collapsed — sitemap.ts called a batched reader. But that batch used `.limit(min(n*200, 5000))` with no `.range()`, and `.limit()` does not raise PostgREST's server-side `max_rows` (supabase/config.toml:18 = 1000, and service_role does not escape it). So it declared a 5000-row appetite, received 1000, and reported no error. Because the batch orders `created_at DESC` ACROSS ALL SPACES, the dropped rows were whole trailing Spaces: their /podcasts index and every Show URL vanished from the sitemap with nothing to notice. Collapsing 200 correct small queries into one truncated one traded latency for missing URLs — the third instance today of a fix whose instrument could not tell 'nothing there' from 'I could not see'. Now paged explicitly with `.range()` over a TOTAL order (created_at DESC, id ASC — the tiebreaker is required so a created_at tie cannot straddle a page boundary and be skipped or repeated), stopping on a short page. Still O(rows), never O(Spaces).

verify.note: Probes the CONSEQUENCE — that the batched read pages — rather than the row's words. Backed by app/sitemap.test.ts, which rebuilds the URL list the old per-Space loop would have emitted and requires an exact match, and which was confirmed to FAIL against an unpaged read (expected 1000 to be 1500) before being accepted.

entries.title: Every Vercel build now throws its cache away: 1.53 GB against a 1.50 GB limit
entries.detail: The build log ends: `Build cache size 1.53 GB exceeds limit of 1.50 GB. Invalidating cache. Next build will start with an empty cache.` It is 2% over, so every build pays a full cold compile and the next one is guaranteed to overflow again — the steady state is no cache at all. entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17 (ADR-1070). check:authz was FILE-level: it saw a gate called somewhere in the file, so an early return before the gate, a gate on one branch of an if, and a gated GET beside an ungated POST all read as green. It now requires EVERY exported HTTP method to pass three structural rules, following the body through a wrapper's local handler (27 cron routes) and into file-local helpers: R1 per-export, R2 the gate is not nested inside if/else/switch/catch, R3 no createAdminClient() query above the gate. R3 IS A DELIBERATE NARROWING AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY. A literal 'any return before the gate' rule was tried against the real corpus first: it fires on 10 of the 52 gated handlers and all ten are validation (400 on a malformed body, 429 on rate limit, an empty list for a blank query). Shipping that would have been 100% false positives on day one, which is the ADR-970 shape - a guard that cannot fire honestly gets routed around and then reads as coverage. What is dangerous is not returning early, it is answering from the service-role client before you know who is asking, and that is what R3 measures. IT FOUND THREE REAL FALSE GREENS, each re-verdicted as a digest-pinned human reading: check-handle (auth.getUser inside an if, over a SECURITY DEFINER RPC) -> public; auth/callback (auth.getUser three branches deep in a swallowed analytics block; the real credential check is exchangeCodeForSession) -> token-credential; q/[slug] (service-role read of the code row before getMyProfileId, which answers WHO scanned, not MAY they) -> self-scoped. entries.title: check:backlog costs 24s and grows ~2s per closed row, because ten probes each spawn a vitest run
entries.detail: MEASURED, not estimated: `node scripts/check-backlog.mjs` takes 23.9s. 21 rows carry a cmd probe and TEN of them spawn a full vitest run to prove their consequence — the honest instrument, and an expensive one. It already turned CI red once: backlog-contract.test.ts's ripgrep-parity arm runs the guard TWICE by design and blew the default 30s test timeout. entries.title: One dropped TCP connection during prerender kills the whole deploy, and nothing retries
entries.detail: OBSERVED, not theorised. The preview build of 656dac3 failed while the PRODUCTION build of the SAME COMMIT succeeded four minutes earlier. The failure: `TypeError: fetch failed / Caused by: Error: read ECONNRESET` on a Supabase read, which the reader wraps as DiscoverReadError and rethrows, and Next reports 'Export encountered an error on /discover/events/[slug]/page: breathe-connect-expand-2026-09-10, exiting the build.' One transient reset on one slug ended the export. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FLAKY PREVIEW: `main` is protected and MERGING DEPLOYS TO PRODUCTION (AGENTS.md). This same read runs during the production export, so the same blip takes down a production deploy, and the only evidence would be a stack trace that looks like a code fault. The build is otherwise healthy - the report says 'No memory or disk space problems detected'. THE FIX IS NOT A BARE try/catch. Swallowing the error would silently ship a /discover with missing events, which is the fail-safe-with-no-gate pattern AGENTS.md names ('every fail-safe needs a gate that notices it fired'). The honest shape is a bounded retry with backoff around the read for RETRYABLE transport faults only (ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, fetch failed), leaving a genuine query error - bad SQL, RLS denial, missing column - fatal exactly as it is now. If a retry is exhausted the build should still fail, loudly, with the slug named. A count of retries consumed belongs in the build log so a rising number is visible before it becomes an outage.

entries.title: /the-lab emits no FAQPage, and has not since its template landed
entries.detail: Found while retiring the-lab's coded body, and it is NOT caused by that retirement. THE_LAB_FAQ carried five Q&A and its faqSchema() call sat on the LEGACY branch of `data ? <BlockRender/> : <Legacy/>` - the branch that could never be taken, because the template is a static literal and `data` is never null. So /the-lab has emitted no FAQPage structured data since the template landed. The retirement deleted the source copy; it did not change what Google sees, which was already nothing. MEASURED, and NARROWER THAN FIRST REPORTED: lib/page-editor/templates/the-quest.ts contains 1 Accordion block and the-lab.ts contains 0. the-quest is therefore FINE - its Accordion emits the FAQPage through BlockDocJsonLd, exactly as its own code comment says. This row is /the-lab alone. THE FIX IS A CONTENT DECISION, not a schema patch: adding faqSchema back without visible Q&A on the page would assert markup for copy a visitor cannot see, which CONTENT-VOICE section 8b forbids and Google penalises. The honest fix is an Accordion block in the-lab's template carrying the five questions, which emits the FAQPage as a consequence of rendering them. That MOVES PIXELS on /the-lab across four skins and two viewports, so it needs a baseline recapture in the same PR. The five drafted answers are good and are preserved in git history at the retirement commit.

entries.title: The AI help index silently stopped re-indexing: every run since 2026-08-13 died before doing any work
entries.detail: help-index.yml re-embeds the help centre into help_chunks on every merge to main touching content/help/**, and runs with NO pnpm install on purpose: the pipeline reads local Markdown with fs and embeds over HTTP. lib/help/content.ts later gained `import { cache } from 'react'` for per-request memoisation - a real win for the app - and from that moment the indexer died on ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'react', imported from lib/help/content.ts, BEFORE reading a single article. MEASURED, not inferred: the six most recent runs on main (2026-08-13 02:32, 03:28, 08-14 01:26, 08-16 19:53, 08-18 03:01) are ALL failure, and the 03:01 log names react explicitly. The secrets ARE configured - the log shows NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY as ***, so it cleared the skip guard and then crashed. Nobody noticed for five days because the help PAGES render straight from Markdown regardless; only AI search went stale, and stale search is indistinguishable from search. FIXED by splitting the dependency-free readers into lib/help/content-core.ts (node builtins only) and leaving cache() in content.ts, which composes it. PROVED by running the indexer in a directory with no node_modules at all: it now resolves every import, parses the content, and reaches the embed HTTP call. OPEN CONSEQUENCE, owner action: this fix does not touch content/help/**, so merging it does NOT trigger a re-index. The index is stale for every help article added or edited since 2026-08-13 until someone runs the workflow once by hand (Actions > help-index > Run workflow).
